actor: Model release engineering lead, open-weights frontier AI lab
job: Shipping the 2.8-trillion-parameter MXFP4 checkpoint with shard layout, deployment guidance and license terms that permit redistributing modified serving artifacts.
outcome: A published checkpoint and license under which third parties may release and redistribute a modified single-node serving recipe.
motivation: Its own hosted tier already paused new subscriptions under inference demand, so serving work must move onto other people's hardware.

task.who: Model release and open-source licensing team
task.what: Publish weights with redistribution-permissive license terms
task.where: Public model hub repository and accompanying model card
task.why: Hosted capacity is capped; external serving relieves demand
task.how: Hugging Face release, MXFP4 shards, published license text

job: Adding an expert-offload execution path that keeps attention and hot experts in accelerator memory while streaming cold experts from host DRAM.
outcome: A merged upstream release serving all 896 experts on eight 80GB cards without pruning, distillation or further quantization.
motivation: Sixteen of 896 experts fire per token, so full HBM residency buys latency rather than correctness and wastes most users' hardware.

task.who: Core runtime and MoE execution maintainers
task.what: Implement per-layer expert offload and residency management
task.where: Upstream inference-engine repository, MoE scheduler and memory allocator
task.why: Residency, not working set, is the real constraint
task.how: Host-DRAM expert cache, pinned buffers, layer-wise prefetch

actor: Low-precision kernel engineer, inference software team
job: Writing MXFP4 weight and MXFP8 activation kernels that run the released precision on accelerators lacking native microscaling-format hardware support.
outcome: Kernels executing the released MXFP4 weights unchanged on widely held 80GB accelerators, so no further quantization is needed.
motivation: Native MXFP4 execution wants Blackwell or MI400 silicon, which the single-node builders chasing this recipe do not own.

task.what: Emulate MXFP4 dequantization in fused GEMM kernels
task.where: Runtime kernel library for prior-generation 80GB accelerators
task.why: Released precision must survive on hardware people own
task.how: CUTLASS or Triton fused dequant-GEMM, block-scale handling

actor: Mixture-of-experts systems researcher, model efficiency group
job: Profiling expert activation locality to decide which experts stay resident and to prefetch the rest from router logits ahead of use.
outcome: A hot-expert residency and prefetch policy that hides most host-to-device transfer behind compute during decode.
motivation: Streaming cold experts naively converts memory-bound decode into something far slower, and bad throughput kills adoption of the recipe.

task.who: Model efficiency research and systems benchmarking group
task.what: Measure expert reuse and build a prefetch policy
task.where: Instrumented decode traces on the published K3 checkpoint
task.why: Throughput, not feasibility, is what stops publication
task.how: Router-logit lookahead, LRU expert cache, activation-frequency profiling

actor: Storage and host-memory data-path engineer, inference infrastructure
job: Building the NVMe and pinned-DRAM streaming path that feeds cold expert weights across PCIe fast enough to keep decode moving.
outcome: A single-node I/O path sustaining expert streaming from host DRAM or NVMe at usable decode throughput.
motivation: The recipe trades HBM capacity for PCIe bandwidth, so the transfer path is where the whole approach succeeds or fails.

task.who: Storage and I/O performance engineering team
task.what: Tune NVMe-to-device expert weight streaming throughput
task.where: Single node with multi-terabyte host DRAM and NVMe
task.why: PCIe bandwidth replaces the HBM capacity given up
task.how: GPUDirect Storage, pinned host buffers, asynchronous copy engines

actor: Single-node deployment engineer, GPU-constrained AI lab
job: Assembling and benchmarking a full-checkpoint serving configuration on one eight-card node, then publishing the configuration, throughput numbers and reproduction steps.
outcome: A public, reproducible recipe serving all 896 experts at released precision within 640GB of accelerator memory.
motivation: They cannot rent sixteen nodes, and must optimize against the single node and host DRAM they actually have.

task.what: Benchmark and publish an eight-card full-weights serving recipe
task.where: Public repository, model hub write-up and technical blog
task.why: Their own constraint is one node, not sixteen
task.how: Docker image, config files, reported tokens-per-second measurements
